messages:
Alex H: hey team — first week here, quick infra question. I'm behind my company proxy and need to run some streaming tests against the sandbox/hosted API. which key should I use for local dev, and do we have static egress IPs I can ask our security team to whitelist? also worried about hitting 429s during burst tests.

Maya R (DevEx): welcome, Alex! :wave: For dev work we usually recommend the sandbox key (it's free and rate-limited differently). Hosted keys are for staging/prod. You can grab a sandbox key from Console > API Keys. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/settings/keys

Maya R (DevEx): about whitelisting — hosted API doesn't guarantee a small, stable set of egress IPs (cloud-managed). For teams that need whitelisting we suggest either: 1) use our devproxy (see below) which has a stable egress IP for your org, or 2) request a dedicated egress range from eng-infra if you're an enterprise/private tenant.

InfraBot: Note: default sandbox quota = 60 requests/minute and streaming connections capped at 8 concurrent per key. If you need a burst test, open a ticket to infra with expected throughput and test windows.

Alex H: ah ok — does the devproxy require special creds? can i run it locally or does it live in a shared subnet?

Sam L: you can run a lightweight local devproxy that forwards requests through our team egress if your SRE grant you access. example quick run (local):
```
docker run -e RW_API_KEY=sandbox_XXXX -p 8080:8080 redwood/devproxy:latest
# then point your app at http://localhost:8080
```
The org-shared devproxy (prod) uses egress 34.122.11.90 that security teams can whitelist. Ping @infra to request access.

Maya R (DevEx): if you can't use devproxy, tell security: we can provide a signed CIDR block request but that takes 1–2 days. Also, for burst tests ask for a temporary quota bump rather than full whitelist; infra will timebox it.

Linda - DevEx: quick note on 429 handling: use exponential backoff + jitter. For streaming, prefer token-based pacing (monitor tokens/second). If you want, share your test script and we can recommend batching/latency knobs to avoid hitting limits.

Alex H: sweet, thank you. i'll try the docker devproxy first and i'll open an infra ticket if I need the org egress. can you tag me when you approve any temp quota bump? @Maya R @Sam L

Maya R (DevEx): will do — tag me in the ticket. :thumbsup:

Sam L: i'll add you to the devproxy access group once you create the infra ticket. :ok_hand:

Alex H: perfect, thanks everyone!
